findings.reason: the node would either write a shrinking fixture that proves nothing about a truncated-and-rewritten stream, or be forced mid-node to change `ingest_stream`'s identity to `file_memo.file_signature` (which already carries size, mtime and ctime) without the plan saying so or declaring a control for it.
findings.text: §6 asserts "a rewritten stream is detected and refolded", but the mechanism the same section states at line 163 — "a stream whose inode changed or that shrank is folded from its start" — cannot detect a rewrite that keeps the inode and grows, which `station_store.ingest_stream` (`reckon/crew/station_store.py:419`–`426`, `if row["inode"] == inode and stored <= st_size`) folds from the stale offset: measured in this workspace with a 354-byte stream rewritten in place to 459 bytes, the incremental observation differs from a full fold of the rewritten file (`rewrite_detected_equals_full_fold False`, `rewrite-probe.log`); because none of the five declared controls mutates the rewrite detector (they cover the stored offset, the carried fold state, classify-every-run, a pointer-and-stream-only change key and the quiet-beat reading), a fixture whose rewrite happens to shrink the file passes the measure while the hazard the line claims to close stays open
